# Didache Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 6

**1** Take care that no one leads you astray from this way of the Teaching — for anyone who does so teaches you apart from God.

**2** If you are able to bear the whole yoke of the Lord, you will be perfect; but if you are not able, do whatever you can.

**3** Regarding food: bear what you are able. But keep entirely away from food sacrificed to idols — for it is the worship of dead gods.

---

*LOGOS notes: V.2's "yoke of the Lord" is a key transition between the Two Ways section (chs. 1–5) and the liturgical section (chs. 7–10). In Jewish usage, "taking the yoke of Torah" meant full covenant observance. The Didache adapts this for a community that likely includes Gentile converts who cannot observe everything. The pastoral accommodation ("do whatever you can") is remarkable and anticipates later catechumenal practice. V.3's grounding of the idol-food prohibition in the theological claim that these gods are "dead" echoes Ps 115:3-8 and early Christian polemic.*
